Why a near-perfect backtest is usually overfit 📉

A smooth equity curve and a tiny drawdown look like a discovery. Most of the time they're just the luckiest result out of many attempts.

In our (hypothetical) simulation, 100 strategy variants with zero real edge still produced a "winner" with an in-sample Sharpe above 1 in 99% of runs. On data it had never seen, that winner averaged zero.
